source.title: Towards a knowledge-enhanced single-cell foundation model
source.authors: Han-Qing Zhang; Jie Bao; Mei Ma; Shuai Liu; Jia-Ying Ma; Jia-Guan Liu; Jia-Xiao Li; Zhen-Bo Li; Wen-Wen Gong; Zhijun Ca

record.tranche_reason: The paper discusses language-model scaling as motivation and reports its own single-cell data-scaling analysis, but it does not test the claim's held-out cross-entropy power laws, extrapolation, compute-optimal allocation, or architecture-shape claim.
record.gate_note: The paper varies the single-cell pretraining corpus size and reports downstream-task performance, not held-out pretraining loss. It does not fit or test power laws, extrapolate losses, or compare parameter-token allocations at fixed compute. Its discussion of a cited evaluation is not a result from this study. The rows record the paper's own related data-scaling results; they do not measure a claim version.
record.test_reason: The study runs its own data-scaling experiment on a single-cell transcriptomic Transformer: nested 10/25/50/100% corpus subsets, trained to validation convergence. It reports only a normalized composite of downstream task scores, not held-out pretraining loss. It fits no power law and varies neither parameters nor compute. The system is not a language model, so no row measures what V1–V7 name. Kaplan et al. is cited only as the LLM contrast.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate. The authors report diminishing downstream gains from corpus expansion and consistent gains from knowledge supervision across scales. They caution that the pattern is specific to their corpus, architecture and benchmarks.
record.recipe_differences: The study uses a single-cell transcriptomic pretraining setup and evaluates downstream metrics over corpus-size fractions; it does not reproduce the language-model loss-scaling method.
record.method_sensitivity: The authors state that the data-efficiency pattern was obtained within a specific combination of pretraining corpus, model architecture, and downstream benchmarks.

fits_no_version.finding: In a single-cell transcriptomic Transformer, mean normalized downstream performance without knowledge supervision plateaued after 50% of a 358k-profile corpus. Knowledge supervision raised scores by an average of 28.8% across the four data scales.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: In single-cell foundation models, downstream performance shows diminishing returns to pretraining corpus size rather than steady scaling. Auxiliary biological supervision shifts the curve upward.

record.problems: The scaling outcomes relevant here are reported as downstream metrics rather than held-out pretraining loss; numerical values for each corpus fraction are not stated in the text. The authors also note that their data-efficiency result is specific to the tested corpus, architecture, and downstream benchmarks.

untested.parts: No held-out pretraining loss versus parameters, tokens or compute is reported.
No fitted law and no extrapolation.
No fixed-compute allocation between parameters and tokens.
Architecture is held fixed (12 layers, 512 hidden).
Pretraining loss in the transcriptomic modality is not reported or fitted against data size.
There is no language-model downstream predictability analysis. The single-cell downstream plateau is outside the version's system kind and gives no loss link.
There is no comparison of fitting choices or exponents.

record.verdict_notes: The scaling range is narrow: one decade of data, about 36k to 358k profiles, at a single model size. Training ran to convergence at each fraction. The study cites DenAdel et al. for a similar scFM plateau, which is not its own result.

versions.untested_parts: Held-out language-model pretraining loss versus parameters, tokens, or compute.
Prediction of larger-run held-out loss from power laws fitted on smaller runs.
Fixed-compute allocation between parameter count and token count.
Loss changes from depth, width, or other architecture details at fixed parameter count.
Whether the same power-law form holds for held-out pretraining loss in another modality or training regime.
Whether language-model downstream performance improves predictably with scale or pretraining loss.
Dependence of fitted language-model scaling exponents or compute-optimal allocation on setup and fitting choices.

rows.subject: scKITE (w/o knowledge enhancement)
rows.operation_detail: Pretrained on nested subsets of the corpus at 10%, 25%, 50%, and 100%; compared aggregate normalized downstream performance across cell annotation, batch integration, and perturbation-response prediction.

conditions.value: cell type annotation, batch integration, genetic perturbation-response prediction

rows.measure: Mean normalized downstream performance across the three tasks
rows.value: Reached a performance plateau after scaling to 50% of the pretraining data, with limited additional gains from further corpus expansion.
rows.locator: Results, “Knowledge-enhanced pretraining improves transcriptomic representations beyond data scaling”; Fig. 1a; Supplementary Methods 5
rows.note: The stated result is about downstream performance versus corpus size, not held-out cross-entropy loss or a fitted power law.
rows.check: The plateau in downstream composite score with corpus size is a related construct: a non-LM system, a downstream metric and no fitted law. No per-fraction numbers are stated in the text (Fig. 1a only). The link to none is correct.

source_check.correct: Link to V6: partial downstream improvement with data scale; scKITE without knowledge enhancement plateaus at 50%, with limited subsequent gains. No fitted law or extrapolation is reported.
source_check.locator_found: Results, first subsection, lines 111–120; Supplementary Methods §5, lines 1378–1450.
source_check.problem: The downstream data-scaling experiment bears on V6; excluding every version and assigning cannot_determine overlooks this evidence.
